quiz.title: Unit 2 SAQ 07
quiz.headline: Comparing land and sea networks
quiz.prompt: Answer all parts of the question. Use evidence from the period c. 1200 to c. 1450.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE similarity between the Silk Roads and Indian Ocean trade networks in the period 1200–1450.
criteria: Names a feature shared by both networks.
Supports it with evidence from each network.

model.answer: Both networks spread religions along with goods.
model.prove: Islam and Buddhism traveled the Silk Roads into Central Asia and China, while Islam spread by sea to Swahili and Southeast Asian ports.
model.explain: In both networks, merchants and teachers who traveled for trade carried beliefs that local communities adopted and adapted.

parts.alternatives: Both carrying luxury goods such as silk and spices, or both depending on trading cities as service nodes, also earns the point.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE difference between the two networks in transport or goods.
criteria: States a specific difference with evidence from both networks.
Explains the consequence of that difference for trade.

model.answer: Indian Ocean ships could carry bulkier, cheaper goods than Silk Roads caravans.
model.prove: Ships moved cargoes such as cotton cloth, timber, and grain, while caravans of camels and horses concentrated on light, valuable goods such as silk.
model.explain: Because sea transport carried more for its cost, the Indian Ocean could support trade in everyday goods as well as luxuries.

parts.alternatives: A difference in the environmental knowledge each required, monsoon winds versus oases and mountain passes, can also work.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE reason for the difference you described in part B.
criteria: Gives a specific cause for the difference.
Explains how the cause produced it.

model.answer: Geography made sea transport cheaper per unit of cargo than overland transport.
model.prove: A single ship using the monsoon winds could carry far more than a caravan, which needed animals, fodder, water, and payments at each oasis.
model.explain: Lower costs per load meant that goods of modest value could still be traded profitably by sea but not across deserts and mountains.

parts.alternatives: If part B compared environmental knowledge, a reason can explain how wind patterns and desert water sources created different planning needs.
